subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which quantity is a vector?
questions.explain: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; distance, speed and time are scalars.

questions.q: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of:
questions.explain: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time, and is itself a vector.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2.0 m/s^2 for 5.0 s. Its final velocity is:
Using v^2 = u^2 + 2as, an object starting from rest and accelerating at 4.0 m/s^2 over 8.0 m reaches a speed of:
On a velocity-time graph, the gradient (slope) represents:
questions.explain: The gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration; the area under it is displacement.

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, the area under the line represents:
questions.explain: Area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement travelled.

questions.q: An object is dropped from rest (take g = 9.8 m/s^2). After 2.0 s its speed is approximately:
questions.explain: v = gt = 9.8 x 2.0 ≈ 20 m/s (ignoring air resistance).

questions.q: For projectile motion (ignoring air resistance), the horizontal and vertical motions are:
questions.explain: Horizontal velocity is constant while vertical motion accelerates under gravity; the two are analysed separately.

questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally from a cliff. Its horizontal velocity during flight (no air resistance):
questions.explain: With no horizontal force, horizontal velocity is unchanged; only the vertical component accelerates.

questions.q: An object falling through air reaches terminal velocity when:
options: The drag force equals its weight
questions.explain: At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero, so acceleration is zero and velocity is constant.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m north then 40 m south. Its displacement is:
questions.explain: Displacement is the net change in position: 100 - 40 = 60 m north; distance would be 140 m.

questions.q: Using s = ut + 0.5at^2, an object at rest accelerating at 3.0 m/s^2 for 4.0 s travels:
Instantaneous velocity is found from a displacement-time graph by taking:
options: The gradient of the tangent at that point
questions.explain: The tangent's gradient gives velocity at an instant; average velocity uses total displacement over total time.

questions.q: At the highest point of a vertically thrown ball's flight, its velocity and acceleration are:
questions.explain: The ball is momentarily at rest but still accelerates downward at g throughout.

questions.q: A negative gradient on a velocity-time graph indicates:
questions.explain: A negative slope means velocity is decreasing (the object is slowing down if moving in the positive direction).

questions.q: A cyclist covers 300 m in 20 s at constant speed. The speed is:
questions.explain: speed = distance ÷ time = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 m/s.

questions.q: The area under an acceleration-time graph gives the:
questions.explain: Integrating acceleration over time yields the change in velocity.

questions.q: A projectile is launched at an angle. Which factor determines its time of flight (level ground, no air resistance)?
options: The vertical component of the initial velocity
questions.explain: Time of flight depends on the vertical launch velocity and g, independent of the horizontal component and mass.

questions.q: Average velocity is defined as:
options: Change in speed divided by time
questions.explain: Average velocity is a vector: total displacement over total time. Average speed uses distance.

questions.q: A train decelerates from 30 m/s to 10 m/s in 5.0 s. Its acceleration is:
questions.explain: a = (v - u)/t = (10 - 30)/5.0 = -4.0 m/s^2 (negative indicates deceleration).
